title: Public-good kits
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for building agent kits that nonprofits can use: need briefs, skill files, read-only tool definitions, prompts, made-up test cases, self-checks, independent review, accessibility and translation checks, and a steward's release decision.
boundaries: Use only made-up, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into a kit, a test case or an output.
Kits stay in the requester's scope. Releasing a kit to others is the steward's separate decision, through the catalog's own reviewed path.
Steps that touch a person's safety, rights or records stay with people.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for building agent kits that nonprofits can use

value.lets_workers: Turn a nonprofit's need into a small, tested kit of agent files: skill instructions, read-only tool definitions, prompts, ready-to-use files and made-up test cases. The drafting worker checks its own work, a different worker reviews it, accessibility and translations are checked, and a person, the steward, decides whether to release it.

flow.when: First: one need, its users and the steps that must stay human.
After the need brief; it proposes write-test-cases.
Made-up cases, including hand-offs and refusals.
By the drafting worker; deterministic checks.
By a different worker than the drafter.
Once per language the need brief lists; each translation is reviewed by a fluent reviewer.
Last: a person decides release or hold.

human_only: Interviewing a client or collecting their story.
Deciding a person's eligibility, benefits or legal position.
Filing anything with a court, agency or funder.
Contacting a person on the organization's behalf.
rules: Use only made-up, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into a kit, a test case or an output.
Kits stay in the requester's scope. Releasing a kit to others is the steward's separate decision, through the catalog's own reviewed path.
Tools are read-only by default; anything with side effects stays a human step.

nouns.title: How to build a kit a nonprofit can trust
nouns.category_reason: A reusable method with its guardrails for every verb in this pack.

rules: Solve one need well; a kit is small enough for a volunteer to understand in ten minutes.
Keep every step in the human_only list with a person, and say so in the skill file.
Tools read; people act. A tool that would write, send or file is a human step instead.
Use only made-up, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into a kit, a test case or an output.
The worker that drafts a kit never reviews it.
Kits stay in the requester's scope. Releasing a kit to others is the steward's separate decision, through the catalog's own reviewed path.
human_only: Interviewing a client or collecting their story.
Deciding a person's eligibility, benefits or legal position.
Filing anything with a court, agency or funder.
Contacting a person on the organization's behalf.

nouns.title: Deterministic self-checks for a kit
nouns.category_reason: A fixed set of checks every kit is scored against before review.

checks.check: Every file in the manifest exists and matches its SHA-256.
Every MCP tool spec validates against template.mcp-tool and is read_only with no side effects.
Every tool's input and output schemas are valid JSON Schema objects.
Every variable a prompt uses is listed, and every listed variable is used.
Every skill names its human handoffs, and every boundary in the need brief appears in the manifest.
Test cases are marked made-up and contain no real names, addresses, phone numbers or case numbers.
Every test case that a deterministic tool can answer was run and matched its expected result.

nouns.title: Accessibility and language criteria for kits
nouns.category_reason: A fixed rubric every kit is checked against before release.

criteria.asks: Instructions read at about a grade 8 level, with terms defined where first used.
Files use real headings and lists, so screen readers can navigate them.
Every image or diagram has a text alternative.
No instruction depends on color alone.
Checklists and directories work when printed in black and white.
Every language the need brief lists has a translated and reviewed version, or is marked pending.

nouns.title: Template: one nonprofit need: who has it, the constraints, how success is measured and which steps stay human

value.describes: one nonprofit need: who has it, the constraints, how success is measured and which steps stay human
rules: One need per brief.
Describe the organization by type, never by name or with real people's details.

example.problem: Volunteers spend the first ten minutes of every call finding which local office handles a repair complaint.
constraints: No client data leaves the call notes system.
Works offline from a printed directory export.
example.success_measure: A volunteer finds the right office in under two minutes on 18 of 20 made-up test calls.
human_boundaries: Interviewing a client or collecting their story.
Deciding a person's eligibility, benefits or legal position.

nouns.category_reason: A need brief frames a falsifiable claim that a kit will help, with a success measure.

nouns.title: Template: a kit manifest: purpose, every file with its digest, human boundaries, license and languages

value.describes: a kit manifest: purpose, every file with its digest, human boundaries, license and languages
rules: Every file is pinned by SHA-256.
human_boundaries repeats the need brief's list.

nouns.category_reason: A kit is a reusable multi-step agent skill bundle with tool bindings and guardrails.

value.describes: a skill file: when to use it, steps, inputs, outputs, guardrails and human hand-offs
rules: Every human_only step appears in human_handoffs.
Steps are short and plain.

nouns.category_reason: A skill file is one reusable agent skill with its guardrails.

nouns.category_reason: An MCP tool definition is a capability card with tool schemas and auth scope.

verbs.title: Frame the need
verbs.summary: Turn a nonprofit's request into one need brief with users, constraints, a success measure and the steps that must stay human.
verbs.outcome: A need brief, or no_change when the request is not something a kit can help with.

slots.name: request
slots.description: Pin of a noun holding the request in the organization's words, with real details removed.

steps: Verify the pin. Describe the organization by type and remove any real person's details.
Name one need and how a volunteer would know the kit helped.
List every step from the method's human_only list that the need touches.
Propose a draft-kit verb with the need brief pinned.
Use only made-up, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into a kit, a test case or an output.

acceptance.check: The brief validates against template.need-brief's schema.
The brief contains no names, addresses, phone numbers or case numbers.
The success measure can be checked with made-up test cases.

verbs.title: Draft the kit files
verbs.summary: Write the skill files, read-only tool definitions, prompts and ready-to-use files a need brief calls for, and a manifest that pins them.
verbs.outcome: A kit manifest and its files, or no_change when an existing kit already meets the need.

slots.name: existing_kits
slots.description: Pins of existing kits to reuse or extend.

steps: Verify the pins. Reuse an existing kit when it fits.
Keep tools read-only. Never let a tool write, send or file anything; make those human hand-offs in the skill file.
Pin every file by SHA-256 in the manifest.
Propose a write-test-cases verb and a self-check verb.
Use only made-up, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into a kit, a test case or an output.
Kits stay in the requester's scope. Releasing a kit to others is the steward's separate decision, through the catalog's own reviewed path.

acceptance.check: The manifest, skills, tools and prompts validate against their templates.
Every tool has read_only true and side_effects none.
Every human boundary from the need brief appears in the manifest and in a skill's hand-offs.
A volunteer could follow the skill files without extra training.

verbs.title: Write made-up test cases
verbs.summary: Write made-up test cases for the kit: normal, edge, must-hand-off, must-refuse and adversarial, each with the expected behavior.
steps: Verify the pins. Cover the success measure, every human hand-off and at least one adversarial input.
Mark the set made-up and invent every detail; never adapt a real case.
Use only made-up, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into a kit, a test case or an output.

acceptance.check: The cases validate against template.test-cases's schema.
There is at least one case of each kind and one per human boundary.
No case contains a real-looking phone number, address or case number.

verbs.title: Self-check the kit
verbs.summary: The drafting worker runs every deterministic self-check on its own kit and fixes what fails before asking for review.
steps: Run every self-check and record the evidence.
passed is true only if every check is pass or not_applicable.
Propose an independent-review verb when every check passes.

acceptance.check: The report validates against template.self-check's schema.
Every self-check appears exactly once.
passed is true exactly when every check is pass or not_applicable.

verbs.title: Review the kit independently
verbs.summary: A different worker than the drafter reviews the kit's files, test cases and self-check, and accepts, asks for revision or rejects.
steps: Confirm you did not draft this kit; otherwise return blocked.
Rerun the self-checks and read every file.
Try the adversarial cases yourself and confirm the hand-offs happen.
Kits stay in the requester's scope. Releasing a kit to others is the steward's separate decision, through the catalog's own reviewed path.

acceptance.check: The review validates against template.review's schema.
The reviewing key differs from the drafter's key.
Every blocker names the file and the fix needed.

verbs.title: Check accessibility and languages
verbs.summary: Check the kit's files against the accessibility and language criteria and say what to fix.
steps: Check every criterion and note where a file falls short.
Mark languages pending when a translation has no fluent review yet.
Propose a translate-kit verb for each missing language.

acceptance.check: The check validates against template.accessibility-check's schema.
Every criterion appears exactly once.
A volunteer with no technical background can follow the files.

verbs.title: Translate the kit
verbs.summary: Translate a reviewed kit into one language, keeping tool names and schemas unchanged, with a glossary for key terms.
verbs.outcome: A translation awaiting a fluent reviewer.

slots.name: kit_manifest
slots.description: Pin of the reviewed kit manifest.

language.description: Target language tag, such as es or pt-BR.

steps: Translate instructions and messages; never translate tool names, schema field names or file formats.
Record each translated file with the digest of its source.
Leave fluent_review pending.
Propose an independent review of the translation by a fluent reviewer.
Use only made-up, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into a kit, a test case or an output.

acceptance.check: The translation validates against template.translation's schema.
Every file's source_sha256 matches a file in the kit manifest.
fluent_review is pending.

verbs.title: Decide release or hold (steward)
verbs.summary: A person, the steward, reads the kit, its self-check, independent review and accessibility check, and decides release or hold.
verbs.outcome: A release record; releasing into a catalog then follows that catalog's own reviewed path.
steps: Read the kit and every report. Release only with a passing self-check, an accepting review and a passing accessibility check.
Write any conditions, such as languages still pending.
Holding is a valid decision; say why.
Kits stay in the requester's scope. Releasing a kit to others is the steward's separate decision, through the catalog's own reviewed path.

acceptance.check: The release record validates against template.release-record's schema.
A release decision cites a passing self-check, an accept review and a passing accessibility check.
steward is human and the submitting key belongs to the steward.
